summary:
Eight binary STL solids and their kinematic manifest are submitted in position 1 with spring coordinates zero. Own checks, not an official verifier run: all meshes load, are consistently oriented closed single solids, have positive volume and fewer than 200000 triangles. All required bearing shifts produce interference, no rest interference exceeds 0.0002 mm3, non-stem parts fit the case, and the stem reaches x=13.1. A geometric least-motion solver using the specified overlap allowance gives 101.88 degrees arbor winding from 360 degrees forward crown (ratio 3.534); the minute wheel stays stationary. Generated face gears and 25-degree involute spur gears were swept through their meshes, including a 0.25-degree crown grid. The radial click's calculated static run-back after 45 degrees winding is 0.261 degree, giving 47.994 hours reserve. AT-2 is marked not_tested because I did not reproduce the exact 40-step tapped, force-coupled rig. The click is mechanically stopped on its rest side, and its radial locking face supplies a holding constraint; this supports a hold prediction but is not the full tap test. The arbor-only 20-degree sweep at 0.5-degree increments clears, and the subsequent 30-degree crown turn winds another 7.00 degrees. Backward crown rotation through 360 degrees clears with the barrel fixed at the calculated holding boundary, by axial clutch overrun; the follow-up 30-degree forward turn winds 5.71 degrees. Clutch ramp and locking-flank force ratios were checked against both supplied friction coefficients. Pulling and pushing were checked at every 0.03 mm increment. At all five test stops, 24-degree turns in either direction clear and do not drive both trains: 0.225 and 0.45 are neutral, and 0.675 and 0.9 set only. At position 1 the forward 24-degree test winds 3.94 degrees and does not set. A sequential 90-degree forward/back setting cycle moves the minute wheel +19.37/-18.72 degrees. The barrel stays held in the setting model. Pushing in after this cycle clears, and a 90-degree winding restart gives 22.83 degrees arbor motion. These pass judgments use the own geometric solver plus analytical Coulomb flank checks; a general force/contact solver was not available in the supplied folder.
Difficulties in order: Boolean-generated face-tooth sweeps made mesh slivers; I replaced them with a sampled generating envelope, cleaned export degeneracies, and reloaded the STLs. Initial flange, setting-gear and guide clashes required separation, a larger setting face wheel, and an open click guide. A 12-tooth clutch could consume the 30-degree restart allowance; I changed it to 24 teeth and checked friction margins. I then reduced mesh density and added axial clearance above the barrel spur to reduce unnecessary contact and computation.
Ambiguities: the exact contact-force solver, tap selection/settling order and numerical definition of least movement are unspecified. on_stem explicitly promises rotation but is less explicit about translation; the stem shoulders physically locate the sliding clutch in either interpretation. Virtual spring loads are supplied by the declared spring mobiles.
Outside access: none
